---
title: Themes
description: Base and five themes, each a small data document solved into light, dark and Darker.
---

A theme is a small data document: a background, an accent and a style. The style covers shape, density, type, borders and surface accents. Every role is solved to the same contrast targets, so every theme reads the same however it looks.

Apps offer light, dark and follow system, with separate light and dark picks. Each app sets its default theme and opts in to the others.

<ThemeGrid />

## Darker

The OLED version of every theme's dark mode, offered for all of them. Every surface drops by 0.045 OKLCH lightness with hues kept, and text and accents stay as they are, so contrast only goes up. Field outlines use the stronger border so they stay visible. The normal dark stays the default.

## Names

One word in Title Case, naming the building itself, its materials or its parts, never people or times of day. They follow Groundwork's name, so if it's renamed, the themes are renamed with it.

## Using a theme

On the web, load `themes.css` and set the theme and mode on any element:

```html
<body data-gw-theme="glazing" data-gw-mode="dark">
```

Leave `data-gw-mode` off to follow the system's light or dark setting. Darker is opt-in with `data-gw-mode="darker"`.

## Your own theme

Themes aren't only the built-in set. A user can upload a theme file, or an agent can write one, and the app applies it at runtime. The document is the same one the core themes use, checked against the same [Schema](/themes/writing-a-theme), so an agent can write a valid one from that page alone.

The app decodes it, solves it into light, dark and Darker, and checks every role against its contrast target, all in the browser with `@timmo001/groundwork-tokens/runtime`. A theme that misses a target is still applied, with the misses shown, as optional themes are.

```ts
import { parseTheme, runtimeTheme } from "@timmo001/groundwork-tokens/runtime";

const parsed = parseTheme(text);

if (parsed._tag === "Success") {
  const { css, checks } = runtimeTheme(parsed.success, "custom");
  // Add css to the page, then set data-gw-theme="custom"
}
```

Where it's kept depends on what the app has. An uploaded theme starts in the browser's local storage, then moves to a profile or the app's own storage when it has one, such as the host machine for an app served from it, so every client of that host gets it. The document is stored, not the solved CSS, so it's solved again when the solver changes.

The runtime defines that store as `ThemeStore`, with `load`, `save` and `clear`. `localThemeStore(key)` is the first tier; an app with a profile or a host passes its own store with the same shape, and nothing else changes:

```ts
import { localThemeStore, type ThemeStore } from "@timmo001/groundwork-tokens/runtime";

const store: ThemeStore = localThemeStore("my-app:theme");
const text = await store.load();
```

### Following Omarchy

An app can follow the desktop's theme by reading an [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org) theme's `colors.toml`, in `~/.config/omarchy/current/theme/` for the one in use. `omarchyTheme(text)` maps it onto a mapped theme in the mode it declares: its backgrounds become the lower, background and raised surfaces, its foregrounds the text and muted text, and its accent and named colors the accent and status roles. The result applies the same way as any other theme, and its contrast misses are shown.

```ts
import { omarchyTheme, runtimeTheme } from "@timmo001/groundwork-tokens/runtime";

const mapped = omarchyTheme(colorsToml, "Gruvbox");

if (mapped._tag === "Success") {
  const { css } = runtimeTheme(mapped.success, "custom");
}
```

A browser can't open a file dialog in a chosen folder, so a web app asks for the file; a desktop app, a TUI or an agent reads the folder directly. An agent can also hand the file to a web app through its [theme tools](/agents#theme-tools).

Try it: design a theme with the controls, upload a theme document or an Omarchy `colors.toml`, or start from the sample, and the preview takes it as you go. Download saves the document, ready to upload elsewhere or hand to an agent. It's kept in this browser's local storage.
